slides.title: One story. Twelve roles. One writer in control.
slides.subtitle: A proposed path from first idea to an accepted, ordered manuscript.
slides.notes: The 12 are proposed agent instances, including the shared Coordinator / Showrunner. The animation is illustrative. The READ CLI can run its three READ agents with an opt-in live model; this does not establish a live twelve-instance product run.

slides.title: The whole route
slides.subtitle: Follow the light through the proposed workflow. Select a stage to jump to its explanation.
slides.notes: The animated light is an illustration. Human gates pause the proposed route. The READ CLI supports opt-in live-model calls for Research, Reader, and Consistency; the complete twelve-role application route is not live.

slides.title: The writer shapes the brief
slides.subtitle: The original idea stays visible while suggestions are decided one by one.
slides.notes: Intake belongs to the shared Coordinator; it does not add a thirteenth agent. Premise and genre are requested, while other details are optional.

slides.title: Evidence before planning
slides.subtitle: Both provider outcomes enter a versioned dossier, then the writer accepts the exact current version.
slides.notes: Provider metadata, permitted text observations, interpretation, and writer choices remain separate. Partial provider results alone cannot open the dossier gate.

slides.title: Three plans. One approved version.
slides.subtitle: Candidate plans share stable facts and chapter assignments. The writer resolves conflicts.
slides.notes: Planning output is candidate material. A specific bible version and beats require explicit writer approval before writer tasks are dispatched.

slides.title: Three chapters in parallel
slides.subtitle: Each writer receives the same approved bible and a different chapter index.
bullets: Join by index at the barrier
slides.notes: The barrier opens only when all three indexed chapter outputs are valid. Completion order does not determine manuscript order.

slides.title: One structured handoff
slides.subtitle: Reader grounds editorial work in the ordered draft and accepted sources.
slides.notes: Reader returns task, userInstructions, sourceReferences, completeness, and version to the Editors. These five groups describe the downstream Reader-to-Editor contract; they are not the user intake fields or the intake helper. A semantic rejection allows one Reader content repair; unresolved failure pauses the branch.

slides.title: Two candidates, checked separately
slides.subtitle: Editors propose changes. Consistency checks each exact proposal version.
bullets: Editor A and Editor B diverge
slides.notes: Each Critic/Editor is one combined instance. The same Consistency instance runs separate checks for proposal A and B; stale reports cannot certify changed content.

slides.title: The writer decides
slides.subtitle: Accept a current proposal, finish with labeled issues, or request a bounded revision.
bullets: Bible changes need a new approval
slides.notes: Acceptance is an authenticated application action against the current base version. Revision never silently changes approved bible facts.

slides.title: An accepted version leaves the system
slides.subtitle: Markdown export uses the ordered accepted version and carries evidence and unresolved issue labels.
slides.notes: A partial or failed branch is not presented as fully verified. This deck is design documentation, not evidence of production readiness or publication.
